free_tier.stated:
Users now have a limit of 200GB for private models and 200GB for private datasets.

Kaggle has also doubled the maximum upload size of public models and datasets from 100GB to 200GB.

per_object_cap.stated: maximum upload size of public models and datasets is 200GB; private models have a limit of 200GB
per_object_cap.notes: Kaggle has also doubled the maximum upload size of public models and datasets from 100GB to 200GB.

retention.notes: unverified: the models documentation and quota announcement state no retention period

egress.terms: Free. Files come from Kaggle's Google-hosted CDN (storage.googleapis.com) with no egress meter. Downloads require a Kaggle API token.

interface_detail: Many developers will need to download models in code outside of Kaggle. There are a few different methods: via the [kagglehub Python library](https://github.com/Kaggle/kagglehub), via our [Kaggle CLI](https://github.com/Kaggle/kaggle-cli), or by calling the API directly.
tooling: kagglehub and the Kaggle API. GET /api/v1/models/google/bert/get returned 200, 72,158 bytes. Datasets: /api/v1/datasets/list returns 200 JSON with totalBytesNullable per dataset. Note the upload side is narrower than the read side — 'The ability to upload models via the Kaggle API was introduced to a select group of Kaggle accounts starting in version 1.5.18', and kagglehub caps at 50 files per repo and auto-zips beyond that.
chaining: This tool allows you to copy model versions from one model to another. You can import versions from any public model or private models where you have collaborator access.

limits.value: maximum upload size of public models and datasets is 200GB; private models have a limit of 200GB

limits_note: Per-object-cap 200 GB and 50 top-level files per dataset. 'A max of 50 top-level files (if you have more, use a directory structure and upload an archive)'. Uploading via the API is write-gated for most accounts. Practical caveat from the docs: archives are uncompressed server-side so their contents are usable in Notebooks, which means the 200 GB is measured on the expanded tree.
reliability_note: Kaggle is Google-owned and long-lived; the risk is policy drift on public storage, not disappearance. The 200 GB private pool is enforced hard ('if you exceed this, either make your datasets public or delete unused datasets').
confidence_note: The Kaggle product announcement was read on 2026-11-09 and states the private and public model and dataset size limits.

surfaced: 'The ability to upload models via the Kaggle API was introduced to a select group of Kaggle accounts starting in version 1.5.18'. Read path is open, write path is not.

PROBED: curl '/api/v1/models/list?search=bert&pageSize=1' -> 200, 184,016 bytes, real model objects. curl '/api/v1/models/google/bert/get' -> 200, 72,158 bytes. curl '/api/v1/datasets/list?search=titanic&pageSize=2' -> 200 with totalBytesNullable present.

opened: 'We have increased the limit on our backend to 50 files. If you are uploading more than 50 files, than kagglehub will automatically create a zip for you.' Confirms the 50-file ceiling is live.
